source: PLAN.md Module 2 - Home checklist by property type

sections.title: All homes
sections.intro: Shape, door, kitchen, bedrooms, surroundings and lucky spots.

sections.title: HDB
sections.intro: HDB-only checks. Cures stay within HDB rules: no structural changes, and never moving the household shelter.

sections.title: Condo
sections.intro: Read in layers: site, tower, stack, then unit.

sections.title: Landed
sections.intro: Gate, plot, slopes and roads. Structural changes are allowed.

sections.title: Buying stage
sections.intro: Do these before paying the option or booking fee.

sections.title: Reno tips
sections.intro: Dates come from the almanac, not AI.

notes.reno_2026: 2026 renovation note: avoid starting hacking in the south (Five Yellow and Grand Duke) and the north (Three Killings). Pick start dates from the almanac.
notes.hdb_cures: HDB cures stay within HDB renovation rules: no structural changes, and the household shelter is never moved or altered.
notes.myths: Myths vs practice: 'south-facing is always best' and lucky numbers matter much less than facing, completion year and surroundings. Crystals do not turn a badly sited home into a good one.
notes.disclaimer: For reflection and entertainment. Not professional advice.

items.question: Is the floor plan roughly square or rectangular?
items.issue: Irregular shape: one or more Bagua sectors may be missing (a cut of about a third of a side counts; a small notch usually does not).
items.cure: Mark the missing sector on the floor plan. Strengthen it with lighting, a mirror on the adjacent wall or zoning furniture rather than rebuilding.
items.cure_hdb: Use lighting, furniture zoning or a mirror on the adjacent wall. No hacking or extending walls.

items.question: Is the south-west corner missing (cut by a yard, bay window or balcony)?
items.issue: Missing south-west: linked to relationships and the mother figure.
items.cure: Brighten the area next to the missing corner with warm light and earth tones; place a pair of objects or a healthy plant there.
items.cure_hdb: Warm lighting and earth-tone décor next to the missing corner. Do not hack or enclose the yard or bay window.

items.question: Does the main door face a neighbour's door directly?
items.issue: Door-to-door clash: opposing doors are said to fight for qi.
items.cure: Keep a solid door, add a door mat and a screen or shoe cabinet just inside to soften the line.
items.cure_hdb: A door mat and an indoor screen or shoe cabinet just inside. Do not change the corridor or the door position.

items.question: Does the main door face a lift, rubbish chute or staircase?
items.issue: Lift or staircase facing the door: qi rushes past or away; a chute brings stale qi.
items.cure: Keep the door closed, use an indoor screen or partition, and keep the entrance well lit.
items.cure_hdb: Indoor screen or shoe cabinet, good entrance lighting. No change to the common corridor.

items.question: Can you see straight from the main door to a window, balcony or back door?
items.issue: Straight line through the home: qi is said to flow out without settling.
items.cure: Break the line with a screen, curtain, console or tall plant between the door and the opening.

items.question: Does the home have two main doors (or a second door used as a main entry)?
items.issue: Two main doors split the 'mouth of qi'.
items.cure: Choose one door as the main entry and use it daily; keep the other for occasional use.

items.question: Is there a long, narrow corridor straight from the entrance?
items.issue: Long entrance corridor speeds qi up instead of letting it settle.
items.cure: Add rugs, artwork or lighting at intervals to slow the corridor; avoid a mirror at the far end.

items.question: Is a toilet or bathroom in the centre of the home?
items.issue: Toilet in the centre (Tai Chi): said to affect the whole household.
items.cure: Keep the door shut, lid down and room dry and bright; add plants or earth-tone items outside it.

items.question: Does a toilet door face the main door, kitchen or a bed?
items.issue: Toilet door facing the main door, kitchen or bed.
items.cure: Keep the toilet door closed; add a door curtain or screen; keep it clean and ventilated.

items.question: Is a toilet in a household member's lucky sector (see the Quick check result)?
items.issue: Toilet in a good-direction sector presses down that person's luck there.
items.cure: Keep it shut and clean; strengthen the person's other good sectors (bed and desk direction).

items.question: Does the stove face, or sit in line with, the main door?
items.issue: Stove facing the main door: wealth and health are said to leak.
items.cure: Place a screen or half-partition between the door and the kitchen, or keep the kitchen door closed.
items.cure_hdb: A screen or sliding kitchen door within renovation rules; do not move gas points without approval.

items.question: Is the stove right next to, or directly facing, the sink or fridge?
items.issue: Fire and water clash between stove and sink or fridge.
items.cure: Keep at least a small gap or a wooden/green element (a board, plant or wooden utensil holder) between them.

items.question: Is there a window (not a solid wall) behind the hob?
items.issue: No solid backing behind the stove.
items.cure: Where possible use a solid backsplash wall; otherwise keep the window closed while cooking and add a solid panel.

items.question: Can the cook NOT see the kitchen entrance while cooking?
items.issue: Cook cannot see who enters (back exposed).
items.cure: Place a small reflective surface (e.g. a shiny hood or splashback) so the entrance is visible.

items.question: Does the stove face a toilet or bedroom door, or share a wall with a toilet?
items.issue: Stove facing or back-to-back with a toilet or bedroom door.
items.cure: Keep those doors closed; add a wooden or plant element between; avoid the stove on the shared wall at the next renovation.

items.question: Is a bed, sofa or desk under a beam?
items.issue: Beam pressing down on a bed, sofa or desk.
items.cure: Move the furniture out from under the beam, or plan a false ceiling to conceal it.

items.question: Does a mirror face the bed?
items.issue: Mirror facing the bed: said to disturb sleep and relationships.
items.cure: Move the mirror or cover it at night (wardrobe mirrors can face inward or be covered).

items.question: Is a bed in line with the bedroom door (feet or head pointing at the door)?
items.issue: Bed in the 'coffin position' in line with the door.
items.cure: Shift the bed diagonally away from the door so you can see the door from bed.

items.question: Is a headboard against a window, or sharing a wall with a toilet, lift shaft or rubbish chute?
items.issue: Headboard without solid support, or backing onto a toilet, lift shaft or chute.
items.cure: Move the bed to a solid wall; if impossible, use a solid padded headboard and keep the other side dry and tidy.

items.question: Is an air-conditioner, ceiling fan, pendant light or storage loft directly over a bed, sofa or desk?
items.issue: Heavy or moving fixture over a bed, sofa or desk.
items.cure: Shift the furniture so the fixture is not directly overhead.

items.question: Does the floor or unit number contain a 4 (or a number you consider unlucky)?
items.issue: Number luck (popular belief): widely used in Singapore buying but much less important than facing, completion year and surroundings.
items.cure: Treat as a preference only; check facing and surroundings first.

items.question: Does the main door or bedroom window face a common corridor?
items.issue: Corridor-facing: foot traffic and noise disturb qi and privacy.
items.cure: Use frosted film or curtains, and a door screen inside.

items.question: Is a road, T-junction or expressway aimed straight at the home?
items.issue: Road aimed at the home ('road arrow').
items.cure: Place a solid screen, plants or a heavy object facing the line; keep curtains on that side.

items.question: Are a hospital, funeral parlour, temple, substation, police station or government building very close or directly in view?
items.issue: Sensitive buildings nearby (popular and form-school belief).
items.cure: Use curtains or plants on that side; weigh the practical impact (noise, traffic) more than the belief.

items.question: Is there open space, a park or water in front of the facing (a 'bright hall')?
items.issue: No bright hall: the facing looks onto a close wall or block.
items.cure: Keep the front area uncluttered and bright inside; favour units with an open outlook when choosing.

items.question: From the window, do you see a narrow gap between two tall blocks?
items.issue: Wind gap ('heaven's cut') between two tall blocks.
items.cure: Use curtains or blinds on that window; place plants or solid décor on the sill.

items.question: From the window, does a neighbour's sharp corner or roof edge point at the home?
items.issue: Sharp corner ('poison arrow') aimed at the home.
items.cure: Keep curtains on that side and place plants or a solid screen to block the line of sight.

items.question: Is there strong glare from glass façades or a pool into the home?
items.issue: Reflected glare (light sha).
items.cure: Use sheer curtains or tinted film on that side.

items.question: Is there constant noise from an MRT line or expressway?
items.issue: Noise and vibration from an MRT line or expressway.
items.cure: Use double-glazed or acoustic windows and heavy curtains; place bedrooms on the quiet side.
items.cure_hdb: Heavy curtains and approved window upgrades only; bedrooms on the quieter side.

items.question: Is the home right at a very close sea or waterfront?
items.issue: Very close open water is sometimes said not to let qi gather.
items.cure: Use curtains and a solid sill feature on the water side; this rule is contested.

items.question: Is a toilet in the unit above directly over your stove, bed or main door, or a bedroom above your kitchen? (assume the repeating stack layout if unknown)
items.issue: Floor-above clash: a fixed clash in stacked blocks.
items.cure: Move the bed or desk away from that spot where possible; this cannot be cured by décor alone.
items.cure_hdb: Shift the bed or desk away from that spot; no structural changes.

items.question: Is the centre of the home taken up by a household shelter, kitchen, toilet or heavy storage?
items.issue: Blocked centre (Tai Chi): the centre should stay open.
items.cure: Keep the centre tidy and uncluttered; move heavy storage elsewhere.
items.cure_hdb: Keep the shelter tidy and clutter-free inside. The household shelter cannot be moved or altered under HDB rules, and the app never suggests it.

items.question: Is there a standalone structural pillar in the living area ('piercing heart')?
items.issue: Standalone pillar in the middle of a room.
items.cure: Soften it with plants or wrap it with a shelf or mirror panels.
items.cure_hdb: Soften it with plants or a non-structural wrap. Do not hack the pillar.

items.question: Is there a long straight line through the home from front to back?
items.issue: Long straight line through the home: qi rushes through.
items.cure: Break the line with furniture, rugs or a screen.

items.question: Is the altar under a beam or air-conditioner, or backing onto/facing a toilet, kitchen, bedroom, store or household shelter?
items.issue: Altar badly placed.
items.cure: Place the altar on a solid, quiet living-room wall, clear of beams, air-conditioners, toilets, the kitchen and bedrooms.

items.question: Is an aquarium or water feature in a bedroom or kitchen, under a beam, or under or next to the altar?
items.issue: Aquarium or water feature misplaced (water–fire clash with the altar).
items.cure: Move it to the living room (often north, south-east or east), away from beams and the altar.

items.question: Is the far-left corner from the main door (Black Hat wealth corner) cluttered or a toilet?
items.issue: Black Hat wealth corner blocked.
items.cure: Keep the far-left corner clear and bright; a healthy plant is a common choice.

items.question: Is the south-east sector (classical wealth area) cluttered or a toilet?
items.issue: Classical south-east wealth area blocked. Flying Star wealth stars are checked separately on the floor reading.
items.cure: Keep the south-east clear and bright; see this year's Flying Stars for the current wealth star.

items.question: Do you want colour advice by sector?
items.issue: Colours by sector are optional and school-dependent; some classical writers say colours are not feng shui.
items.cure: Treat colour tips as optional; prioritise layout and facing.

items.question: Are you unsure whether to read the facing from the main door or the balcony / living-room window?
items.issue: Facing method unclear: many masters use the balcony or living-room opening; others use the main door.
items.cure: Run the Quick check with 'Not sure — show both' to see both results.

items.question: Is this a corner, jumbo or lift-lobby unit?
items.issue: Special unit: the stack-wide reading may not apply.
items.cure: Take a compass reading at this unit's own opening rather than assuming the stack facing.

items.question: Do a bay window or yard create a cut-out corner?
items.issue: Bay window or yard creating a missing corner.
items.cure: Brighten the adjacent area with lighting or décor. Do not hack or enclose them.

items.question: Does the living room face west (afternoon sun)?
items.issue: West-facing living room: year-round afternoon heat.
items.cure: Use blinds, UV film and light colours; plan the sofa away from direct sun.

items.question: Is the unit on a very high, windy floor?
items.issue: Very high, windy floor; mid floors are often preferred.
items.cure: Use heavier curtains and window stoppers; keep doors from slamming.

items.question: (Resale) Has the layout been changed from the original HDB plan?
items.issue: As-built layout differs from the original HDB plan: the chart stays with the building but which sectors are lived in can change.
items.cure: Compare the as-built layout with the original HDB plan and re-mark rooms on the floor reading. Use the lease commencement year as the completion year.

items.question: Do stacks in this project face different ways?
items.issue: Stacks face different ways: one tower facing does not apply to every unit.
items.cure: Read in layers: site, tower, stack, then this unit's own facing.

items.question: Are the main entrance or drop-off awkward (aimed at the block, or a driveway mouth below the unit)?
items.issue: Main entrance, drop-off or driveway mouth pressing on the unit.
items.cure: Prefer stacks away from the driveway mouth; use curtains on that side.

items.question: Does the pool or water feature sit in front of this stack?
items.issue: Pool position: helps some stacks and burdens others depending on the unit's chart.
items.cure: Check where the water sits on this unit's Flying Star chart before deciding.

items.question: Is the unit over a transfer deck, driveway mouth or substation?
items.issue: Unit over a transfer deck, driveway mouth or substation.
items.cure: Consider another stack or floor; keep the bedroom away from that side.

items.question: From this floor (not the showflat), can you see a sharp corner of another tower?
items.issue: Sharp tower corner visible only from this floor.
items.cure: Visit the actual floor; use curtains or plants to block the line if you buy.

items.question: Is the main gate misaligned with the front door or blocked?
items.issue: Main gate and front door not working together.
items.cure: Check the gate facing as well as the door; keep the path between them clear. Structural changes are possible for landed homes.

items.question: Is the plot irregular (triangular, narrowing at the back)?
items.issue: Irregular plot shape.
items.cure: Use landscaping, fencing or planting to square off the plot.

items.question: Is the house lower than the road, or lacking support at the back (slope down behind)?
items.issue: House lower than the road, or no backing behind the house.
items.cure: Add a solid fence, hedge or tall planting at the back; improve drainage at the front.

items.question: Does a staircase face the main door directly?
items.issue: Staircase facing the main door: qi rushes upstairs.
items.cure: Add a screen or turn the bottom steps; renovation can reposition the stair.

items.question: Is the front door in a straight line with the back door or a rear window?
items.issue: Front door in line with the back door.
items.cure: Place a screen, plants or furniture between them, or move a door during renovation.

items.question: Does a neighbour's roof corner, lamp post, tree, chimney or gate point at the door or windows?
items.issue: Pointing object aimed at the house.
items.cure: Use planting, a screen or a solid gate to block the line.

items.question: Is the house at a Y-junction or inside an inverted-U road?
items.issue: Y-junction or inverted-U road.
items.cure: Plant hedges or a solid fence on the road side.

items.question: Is there a drain or canal in front, or water at the back?
items.issue: Drain or canal in front, or water at the back.
items.cure: Keep drains clean; move ponds or water features to the front instead of the back.

items.question: Is the house sandwiched between taller buildings, or is the fence higher than the house?
items.issue: House pressed between taller buildings, or fence taller than the house.
items.cure: Keep the frontage open and bright; lower the fence where allowed.

items.question: Is the master bedroom above the garage?
items.issue: Master bedroom over the garage (empty, moving space below).
items.cure: Use another room as the master or keep the garage tidy and the floor well insulated.

items.question: Is the house at a cul-de-sac or dead end?
items.issue: Cul-de-sac: contested. Some classical lists treat it as unfavourable; some agents say judge turning space and congestion instead.
items.cure: Judge on traffic and turning space rather than a blanket no.

items.question: Have you checked the centre of each storey, and re-read the chart after any extension or A&A?
items.issue: Centre of each storey or post-extension chart not checked.
items.cure: Check the centre of every storey and re-read the chart after extensions or A&A works.

items.question: Do you have the completion/TOP date and the unit facing in writing?
items.issue: TOP date or facing not confirmed in writing.
items.cure: Ask the agent or developer for the TOP date and facing in writing before paying the option or booking fee.

items.question: Have you checked the URA Master Plan for future buildings in front?
items.issue: View not checked against the URA Master Plan: a good view can be built out.
items.cure: Check the URA Master Plan before committing.

items.question: Have you taken a compass reading on site, held level and away from window grilles?
items.issue: Facing not verified on site.
items.cure: Use the Direction calculator on site, phone flat, away from grilles, three readings.

items.question: Are you doing this check before paying the option or booking fee?
items.issue: Check done after paying the option or booking fee.
items.cure: Do the feng shui check before you pay the option or booking fee.

items.question: Have you aligned the home with each occupant's BaZi or Kua (not just a couple Kua match to the door)?
items.issue: Only a door-to-Kua match was done.
items.cure: Use the BaZi screen or a master consult for a fuller match.

items.question: Are you planning to start hacking or major works in the south sector in 2026?
items.issue: 2026: avoid starting hacking in the south (Five Yellow and Grand Duke).
items.cure: Start works in another sector first, or wait for a better year or date from the almanac.

items.question: Are you planning to start hacking or major works in the north sector in 2026?
items.issue: 2026: avoid starting hacking in the north (Three Killings).
items.cure: Start works in another sector first, or pick a date from the almanac.

items.question: Are works due to start in the Hungry Ghost month (7th lunar month)?
items.issue: Starting works in Hungry Ghost month is commonly avoided.
items.cure: Start before or after the 7th lunar month; check the almanac for a good start date.

items.question: Will the main door or kitchen be left unfinished for a long stretch?
items.issue: Main door or kitchen left unfinished for long.
items.cure: Schedule the main door and kitchen to finish early.

items.question: Will the feng shui check be done before the interior-design drawings are fixed?
items.issue: Feng shui checked after ID drawings: door swing, stove, beds and desks may already be fixed.
items.cure: Do the feng shui check before the ID drawings.

items.question: Did beams appear after hacking that will sit over a bed, sofa or desk?
items.issue: Exposed beams over furniture after hacking.
items.cure: Plan a false ceiling now, before the furniture goes in.

items.question: Are you combining two bedrooms (which may change which room counts as the master)?
items.issue: Combining rooms can change which room counts as the master (often the largest).
items.cure: Re-mark rooms on the floor reading after combining and check whose bed goes where.

items.question: Is the renovation major (roof, floor and main door)?
items.issue: Some lineages say substantial works can reset the period; others say ordinary renovation does not. The app does not auto-reset the period.
items.cure: Ask a master whether your works count; the app keeps the original period unless you change it.

items.question: Have you picked a move-in date and house-warming checklist?
items.issue: Move-in date not chosen.
items.cure: Pick an auspicious date from the almanac that does not clash with household zodiacs. Optional rituals: open windows, light the stove, bring in rice, salt and red dates.
